chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v01] Salutation to the pure mother and five-faced father whose union pulses as the supreme nectar-family heart.

[tal-a01-v10] Victorious are those descended from Shri Somananda, Bodha, and Shrimad Utpala, whose consciousness-bliss compositions spread in all directions.

[tal-a01-v02] I bow to the supreme goddess, Bhairava yogini, established in measureless trident-lotus power.

[tal-a01-v03] I bow to the goddess dwelling in the body, delighting like lightning in rain clouds, in Bhairava's dancing form.

[tal-a01-v04] Pulsing is that knowledge-trident, blazing light that burns the triad of bonds and cuts both true and opposite sides.

[tal-a01-v05] Freedom-power, sequence-creation-desire, and sequence-selfhood are the lord's glory; that goddess triad reveals my supreme own-form.

[tal-a01-v06] Ganapati, goddess-son with moon radiance, fully stirs my ocean of consciousness.

[tal-a01-v07] He who scattered attachment-red knots made the external path artificial; may that pleased lord of my will be gracious.

[tal-a01-v08] Victorious are the former teachers, bearing distinction of the three-eyed named lineage, helmsmen of the scripture-ocean's playful waves.

[tal-a01-v09] Victorious is the one teacher, famous Shrikantha on earth, and his other forms Maheshvara and Bhutiraja.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v11] We bow to the mind-bee of teacher Lakshmanagupta, expanded by fullness of taste and deluding by sound.

[tal-a01-v12] He who rests in full bliss and has crossed all scripture meanings, Shri Cukhulaka, is my best teacher.

[tal-a01-v13] May Shambhunatha, one with the goddess, be victorious; by his teaching rays this difficult scripture path becomes manifest.

[tal-a01-v14] There are various methods in stream divisions, but in the supreme six-half meaning order only one is seen.

[tal-a01-v15] Thus, often requested by good students and fellow students, I compose this clear procedure of full meaning.

[tal-a01-v16] From the lotus feet of Shri Bhattanatha and Shri Bhattarika, Abhinavagupta, bright with knowledge risen from worship that removes other bonds and poison, does this.

[tal-a01-v17] Nothing exists here that is not declared by the god of gods in Shri Malinivijayottara, by his own word and by sign.

[tal-a01-v18] The lord's teaching, distinct in ten, eighteen, six, and eight, has its essence in Trika scripture; that essence is the Malini view.

[tal-a01-v19] Therefore, abandoning tradition, we wise ones make manifest what is unseen, by the command of the guru lord.

[tal-a01-v20] This is the work of Abhinavagupta, whose fame, named by teachers, is obtained through meditation on the lotus feet of the three-eyed one.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tadāsvādabharāveśabṛṃhitāṃ matiṣaṭpadīm / gurorlakṣmaṇaguptasya nādasaṃmohinīṃ numaḥ yaḥ pūrṇānandaviśrāntasarvaśāstrārthapāragaḥ / sa śrīcukhulako diśyādiṣṭaṃ me gururuttamaḥ jayatājjagaduddhṛtikṣamo@sau bhagavatyā saha śaṃbhunātha ekaḥ / yadudīritaśāsanāṃśubhirme prakaṭo@yaṃ gahano@pi śāstramārgaḥ santi paddhatayaścitrāḥ srotobhedeṣu bhūyasā / anuttaraṣaḍardhārthakrame tvekāpi nekṣyate ityahaṃ bahuśaḥ sadbhiḥ śiṣyasabrahmacāribhiḥ / arthito racaye spaṣṭāṃ pūrṇārthā prakriyāmimām śrībhaṭṭanāthacaraṇābjayugāttathā śrībhaṭṭārikāṃghriyugalādgurusantatiryā / bodhānyapāśaviṣanuttadupāsanotthabodhojjvalo@bhinavagupta idaṃ karoti na tadastīha yanna śrī-mālinīvijayottare / devadevena nirdiṣṭaṃ svaśabdenātha liṅgataḥ daśāṣṭādaśavasvaṣṭabhinnaṃ yacchāsanaṃ vibhoḥ / tatsāraṃ trikaśāstraṃ hi tatsāraṃ mālinīmatam ato@trāntargataṃ sarva saṃpradāyojjhitairbudhaiḥ / adṛṣṭa prakaṭīkurmo gurunāthājñayā vayam abhinavaguptasya kṛtiḥ seyaṃ yasyoditā gurubhirākhyā / trinayanacaraṇasaroruhacintanalabdhaprasiddhiriti

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v21] Examine this heart-lotus of Abhinavagupta, whose contraction has gone through the radiance of falling at the feet of Shri Shambhunatha sun, for the worship of Mahesha.

[tal-a01-v22] Here the first statement sung in all scriptures is: ignorance is the cause of samsara, knowledge is the only cause of liberation.

[tal-a01-v23] They desire impurity-ignorance as the cause of samsara's sprout; thus it is declared in Shri Malinivijayottara.

[tal-a01-v24] By qualification established in mind, after samsara, removing possibility in its absence, liberation is declared.

[tal-a01-v25] Ignorance is not just the absence of knowledge, because that would apply too widely. For such absence exists even in a clod of earth, yet a clod does not undergo transmigration.

[tal-a01-v26] Therefore, ignorance is knowledge itself that fails to manifest the knowable reality in its fullness; this is what has been taught in the Shiva Sutras.

[tal-a01-v27] In the two sutras, 'Consciousness is the Self' and 'Knowledge is bondage,' the intended meaning is shown through their mutual relation of connection and separation.

[tal-a01-v28] The word 'consciousness,' by its form, always signifies sheer freedom without implying any particular distinction, as used in the ancient sutra.

[tal-a01-v29] But the second sutra, by speaking of action or instrument, introduces duality into that which is essentially mere consciousness.

[tal-a01-v30] The manifestation of duality is ignorance; because it is insubstantial, it is called bondage, and for that very reason it is shown to be something that must be completely cut off.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-śrīśambhunāthabhāskaracaraṇanipātaprabhāpagatasaṃkocam / abhinavaguptahṛdambujametadvicinuta maheśapūjanahetoḥ ādivākyaṃ iha tāvatsamasteṣu śāstreṣu parigīyate / ajñānaṃ saṃsṛterheturjñānaṃ mokṣaikakāraṇam malamajñānamicchanti saṃsārāṅkurakāraṇam / iti proktaṃ tathā va śrīmalinīvijayottare viśeṣaṇena buddhisthe saṃsārottarakālike / saṃbhāvanāṃ nirasyaitadabhāve mokṣamabravīt ajñānamiti na jñānābhāvaścātiprasaṅgataḥ / sa hi loṣṭādike@pyasti na ca tasyāsti saṃsṛtiḥ ato jñeyasya tattvasya sāmastyenāprathātmakam / jñānameva tadajñānaṃ śivasūtreṣu bhāṣitam caitanyamātmā jñānaṃ ca bandha ityatra sūtrayoḥ / saṃśleṣetarayogāśyāmayamarthaḥ pradarśitaḥ caitanyamiti bhāvāntaḥ śabdaḥ svātantryamātrakam / anākṣipraviśeṣaṃ sadāha sūtre purātane dvitīyena tu sūtreṇa kriyāṃ vā karaṇaṃ ca vā / bruvatā tasya cinmātrarūpasya dvaitamucyate dvaitaprathā tadajñānaṃ tucchatvādbandha ucyate / tata eva samucchedyamityāvṛttyānirūpitam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v31] Anything apart from the free Self is insubstantial, and even such an insubstantial thing cannot be called liberation; it does not even receive a separate name.

[tal-a01-v32] But the knowledge that manifests the true knowable reality in ever fuller measure, rising higher and higher, brings the quieting of each corresponding level of transmigration.

[tal-a01-v33] The knowledge 'I am untainted by passion and the like, inwardly empty, and devoid of limited agency,' whether held briefly or in detail, liberates one to that extent.

[tal-a01-v34] Thus, one who is liberated in one respect but still stands within another limitation is not truly liberated; only one free from all limitations is truly liberated.

[tal-a01-v35] But the knowledge of the true knowable reality that is completely free from all limitations leaves no room anywhere for ignorance and gives true liberation.

[tal-a01-v36] The nature of knowledge and ignorance described above is, in the Shaiva teaching, further divided in each case into two kinds: the personal and the cognitive.

[tal-a01-v37] In that division, the person's ignorance is called impurity; arising from it and dissolving into it, its nature is to veil one's own full Shiva-state of perfect consciousness and action.

[tal-a01-v38] That ignorance of the bound soul has the form of contracted knowing and doing, yet it is non-conceptual, because determinate intellectual operations such as judgment have not yet arisen.

[tal-a01-v39] When, through reflection arising from the limited self within the cavity of the six sheaths, there arises a determining cognition of the form 'I know this in this way'—

[tal-a01-v40] When such intellect arises, that kind of knowledge is called cognitive ignorance; in relation to it, the personal ignorance is both nourished and nourishing.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-svatantrātmātiriktastu tuccho@ tuccho@pi kaścana / na mokṣo nāma tannāsya pṛthaṅnāmāpi gṛhyate yattu jñeyasatattvasya pūrṇapūrṇaprathātmakam / taduttarottaraṃ jñānaṃ tattatsaṃsāraśāntidam rāgādyakaluṣo@smyantaḥśūnyo@haṃ kartṛtojjhitaḥ / itthaṃ samāsavyāsābhyāṃ jñānaṃ muñcati tāvataḥ tasmānmukto@pyavacchedādavacchedāntarasthiteḥ / amukta eva muktastu sarvāvacchedavarjitaḥ yattu jñeyasatattvasya jñānaṃ sarvātmanojjhitam / avacchedairna tatkutrāpyajñānaṃ satyamuktidam jñānājñānasvarūpaṃ yaduktaṃ pratyekamapyadaḥ / dvidhā pauruṣabauddhatvabhidoktaṃ śivaśāsane tatra puṃso yadajñānaṃ malākhyaṃ tajjamapyaya / svapūrṇacitkriyārūpaśivatāvaraṇātmakam saṃkocidṛkkriyārūpaṃ tatpaśoravikalpitam / tadajñānaṃ na budghyaṃśo@dhyavasāyādyabhāvataḥ ahamitthamidaṃ vedmītyevamadhyavasāyinī / ṣaṭkañcukābilāṇūtthapratibimbanato yadā dhīrjāyate tadā tādṛgjñānamajñānaśabditam / bauddhaṃ tasya ca tatpauṃsnaṃ poṣaṇīyaṃ ca poṣṭṛca

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v41] But when the bound soul's conditioning has diminished and the person has reached a higher state, there arises an expansive, non-conceptual personal liberating insight.

[tal-a01-v42] To the extent that expansive non-conceptual knowledge is present, the corresponding cognitive knowledge remains, as before, both nourished by and nourishing the personal knowledge.

[tal-a01-v43] Although personal ignorance may be destroyed by initiation and the like, that knowledge becomes clearly manifest at the end of that body.

[tal-a01-v44] But when the expansion of cognitive ignorance dissolves through cognitive knowledge, liberation while living stands right in the palm of one's hand.

[tal-a01-v45] Initiation too is truly liberating when it is preceded by cognitive liberating insight; therefore, even there, cognitive knowledge has primacy.

[tal-a01-v46] This twofold division within knowledge and ignorance has been taught in the Svayambhuva, the Ruru, the Matanga and others, and by revered teachers such as Khetapala.

[tal-a01-v47] For attaining that cognitive liberating insight which takes the form of such determinate understanding, scripture alone is primary, because it reveals the knowable reality.

[tal-a01-v48] Even when inner personal ignorance has fallen away through initiation, conceptualization may still arise, because what resides in the intellect has not yet ceased.

[tal-a01-v49] Because the mind takes the self to last only as long as the body exists, there would be no liberation even at the end of the body, since human ignorance would still not have been removed.

[tal-a01-v50] But when Buddhist ignorance ceases through the uprooting of conceptualization, liberation occurs right then; this is what the author stated in the revered Niśāṭana.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-kṣīṇe tu paśusaṃskāre puṃsaḥ prāptaparasthiteḥ / vikasvaraṃ tadvijñānaṃ pauruṣaṃ nirvikalpakam vikasvarāvikalpātmajñānaucityena yāvasā / tadbauddhaṃ yasya tatpauṃsnaṃ prāgvatpoṣyaṃ ca poṣṭṛ ca tatra dīkṣādinā pauṃsnamajñānaṃ dhvaṃsi yadyapi / tathāpi taccharīrānte tajjñānaṃ vyajyate sphuṭam bauddhajñānena tu yadā bauddhamajñānajṛmbhitam / vilīyate tadā jīvanmuktiḥ karatale sthitā dīkṣāpi bauddhavijñānapūrvā satyaṃ vimocikā / tena tatrāpi bauddhasya jñānasyāsti pradhānatā jñānājñānāgataṃ caitaddvitvaṃ svāyambhuve rurau / mataṅgādau kṛtaṃ śrīmatkheṭapālādidaiśikaiḥ tathāvidhāvasāyātmabauddhavijñānasampade / śāstrameva pradhānaṃ yajjñeyatattvapradarśakam dīkṣayā galite@pyantarajñāne pauruṣātmani / dhīgatasyānivṛttatvādvikalpo@pi hi saṃbhaveta dehasadbhāvaparyantamātmabhāvo yato dhiyi / dehānte@pi na mokṣaḥ syātpauruṣājñānahānitaḥ bauddhājñānanivṛttau tu vikalponmūlanāddhruvam / tadaiva mokṣa ityuktaṃ dhātrā śrīmanniśāṭane

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v51] A mind still caught in conceptualization would reach Śiva only when the body falls, but the other would reach Śiva right then; this is so because scripture holds primacy here.

[tal-a01-v52] Indeed, the supreme reality to be known is Śiva, whose very nature is light; for what is not luminous cannot be manifest, nor can it even be a real thing.

[tal-a01-v53] Even the non-thingness of beings belongs only to the field of conscious wonder; since it is not like an inert wall, even the thought 'this is unreal' depends on awareness.

[tal-a01-v54] This light shines everywhere and cannot be denied; so what use is there in inventing proofs for it?

[tal-a01-v55] Even the means of knowledge that give life to the knowledge of things have a supreme life of their own, and that is none other than the supreme Lord.

[tal-a01-v56] Even the bold claim that denies everything still operates in this way: the statement 'knowledge is not for the self' appears to me, and so it cannot escape awareness.

[tal-a01-v57] Whether things are denied or established, such a primal ground is already there; so what use do the means of knowledge and their justifications have in that case?

[tal-a01-v59] For that reason, the Kāmika states, without resorting to causal argument, that the God beyond gods has no dependence on anything else.

[tal-a01-v60] Because others depend on the supreme, it stands as independent; for that independent and sovereign reality, the orders of place, time, and form do not apply as limiting conditions.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-vikalpayuktacitastu piṇḍapātācchivaṃ brajet / itarastu tadaiveti śāstrasyātra pradhānataḥ jñeyasya hi paraṃ tattvaṃ yaḥ prakāśātmakaḥ śivaḥ / nahyaprakāśarūpasya prākāśyaṃ vastutāpi vā avastutāpi bhāvānāṃ camatkāraikagocarā / yatkuḍyasadṛśī neyaṃ dhīravastvetadityapi prakāśo nāma yaścāyaṃ sarvatraiva prakāśate / anapahnavanīyatvāt kiṃ tasminmānakalpanaiḥ pramāṇānyapi vastūnāṃ jīvitaṃ yāni tanvate / teṣāmapi paro jīvaḥ sa eva parameśvaraḥ sarvāpahnavahevākadharmāpyevaṃ hi vartate / jñānamātmārthamityetanneti māṃ prati bhāsate apahnutau sādhane vā vastūnāmādyamīdṛśam / yattatra ke pramāṇānāmupapattyupayogite [58 missing] kāmike tata evoktaṃ hetuvādavivarjitam / tasya devātidevasya parāpekṣā na vidyate parasya tadapekṣatvātsvatantro@yamataḥ sthitaḥ / anapekṣasya vaśino deśakālākṛtikramāḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v61] Shiva is not fixed or limited. He is all-pervading and eternal, and he takes the form of the whole universe. Because he pervades everything, he is present everywhere; because he is eternal, he has no beginning or end.

[tal-a01-v62] Because Shiva takes the universe as his form, he appears as the full variety of conscious and unconscious things. For this reason, texts such as the Dikshottara say that he has many forms.

[tal-a01-v63] Shiva is said to appear in six ways: as the world, as a body, as light, as space, as sound, and as mantra. The mantric form also includes bindu, nada, and related expressions.

[tal-a01-v64] Whoever becomes firmly established in a particular nature comes to share in that state. Since space, sound, and related forms are ways Shiva appears, true knowledge of them leads to supreme liberation without doubt.

[tal-a01-v65] The Lord's having the universe as his form is only an indication of his nature. Even when he appears in limited forms, those limits dissolve within his unlimited being.

[tal-a01-v66] The Kamika says that the Lord has all forms and yet is also formless. Like water or a mirror, he pervades everything, both moving and unmoving.

[tal-a01-v67] Qualities such as pervasion and the rest are not really separate in Shiva. They are not divided from one another, but operate as one single quality that includes everything.

[tal-a01-v68] So the straightforward conclusion is that Shiva is endowed with the power of freedom. Even when he is said to have many powers, those powers are not separate from that one power.

[tal-a01-v69] Power is simply a being's own form as it is projected by the knowing subject. For that reason, Shiva remains nondual even when he is thought of as possessing power.

[tal-a01-v70] When the Lord appears in different bodies as projected by the knowing subject, there is no real difference between them. It is like fire, which remains one whether it is burning or cooking.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-niyatā neti sa vibhurnityo viśvākṛtiḥ śivaḥ / vibhutvātsarvago nityabhāvādādyantavarjitaḥ viśvākṛtitvāccidacittadvaicitryāvabhāsakaḥ / tato@sya bahurūpatvamuktaṃ dīkṣottarādike bhuvanaṃ vigraho jyotiḥ khaṃ śabdo mantra eva ca / bindunādādisaṃbhinnaḥ ṣaḍvidhaḥ śiva ucyate yo yadātmakatāniṣṭhastadbhāvaṃ sa prapadyate / vyomādiśabdavijñānātparo mokṣo na saṃśayaḥ viśvākṛtitve devasya tadetaccopalakṣaṇam / anavacchinnatārūḍhāvavacchedalaye@sya ca uktaṃ ca kāmike devaḥ sarvākṛtirnirākṛtiḥ / jaladarpaṇavattena sarvaṃ vyāptaṃ carācaram na cāsya vimutādyo@yaṃ dharmo@nyonyaṃ vibhidyate / eka evāsya dharmo@sau sarvākṣepeṇa vartate tena svātantryaśaktyaiva yukta ityāñjaso vidhiḥ / bahuśaktitvamapyasya tacchaktyaivāviyuktatā śaktiśca nāma bhāvasya svaṃ rūpaṃ mātṛkalpitam / tenādvayaḥ sa evāpi śaktimatparikalpane mātṛklṛpte hi devasya tatra tatra vapuṣyalam / ko bhedo vastuto vahnerdagdhṛpaktṛtvayoriva

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v71] In the highest sense, Shiva is nothing other than manifestation itself. There is no real thing apart from that shining, and there is no ultimately real difference between his power and the one who possesses it.

[tal-a01-v72] Whatever brings forth the surge of a reality's own power is not different from that reality, because it is identical with it. That is power, and in this way the Goddess appears with another form even while remaining the same reality.

[tal-a01-v73] Shiva, whose majesty never fades, appears as if created within the sprout of his own awareness, through his freedom in acts such as contemplation.

[tal-a01-v74] Therefore, although the reality is partless, it shines through particular aspects; that aspect is called its power, yet the power is the reality itself, so the sequence of power and possessor is only an apparent distinction.

[tal-a01-v75] In the revered Kirana scripture, through a question-and-answer discussion, it is stated that neither experience nor mental conceptual thought exists in Shiva, for mind itself is not there.

[tal-a01-v76] To the question, 'How can initiation happen without knowing Shiva?', the answer is that it is not through ordinary experiences like hunger, nor through mental conceptual thought.

[tal-a01-v77] Just as one can recognize a tree from its form even without perceiving its taste and other qualities, so too one can come to know Shiva through indicators such as nada, bindu, and the like.

[tal-a01-v78] Shiva is said to have manifold powers, and from that arises the vast expansion of divisions such as kala, tattva, body, syllable, atom, word, and so on.

[tal-a01-v79] Creation, maintenance, concealment, withdrawal, grace, and even the fourth state are all the unfolding of the Lord's manifold powers.

[tal-a01-v80] Waking, dream, deep sleep, the fourth, and even what lies beyond them are all waves in the abundant freedom of that Lord.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-na vāsau paramārthena na kiṃcidbhāsanādṛte / nahyasti kiṃcittacchaktitadvadbhedo@pi vāstavaḥ svaśaktyudrekajanakaṃ tādātmyādvastuno hi yat / śaktistadapi devyevaṃ bhāntyapyanyasvarūpiṇī śivaścāluptavibhavastathā sṛṣṭo@vabhāsate / svasaṃvinmātṛmakure svātantryādbhāvanādiṣu tasmādyena mukhenaiṣa bhātyanaṃśo@pi tattathā / śaktirityeṣa vastveva śaktitadvatkramaḥ sphuṭaḥ śrīmatkiraṇaśāstre ca tatpraśnottarapūrvakam / anubhāvo vikalpo@pi mānaso na manaḥ śive avijñāya śivaṃ dīkṣā kathamityatra cottaram / kṣudhādyanubhavo naiva vikalpo nahi mānasaḥ rasādyanadhyakṣatve@pi rūpādeva yathā tarum / vikalpo vetti tadvattu nādabindvādinā śivam bahuśaktitvamasyoktaṃ śivasya yadato mahān / kalātattvapurārṇāṇupadādirbhedavistaraḥ sṛṣṭisthititirodhānasaṃhārānugrahādi ca / turyamityapi devasya bahuśaktitvajṛmbhitam jāgratsvapnasuṣuptānyatadatītāni yānyapi / tānyapyamuṣya nāthasya svātantryalaharībharaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v81] The great lords of mantra, the lords of mantra, the mantras headed by Shiva, and the two akala classes together with the sakala class are all powers of Shiva himself.

[tal-a01-v82] The unfailing essential nature of the whole group of principles is the Self alone, for as the revered Trishiro doctrine states, the Self is their very nature.

[tal-a01-v83] By the term 'group of principles' is meant that which stands in the heart, in all bodies, and in its own nature, which is very subtle, and which is the collective totality of the principles.

[tal-a01-v84] The Self alone is said to be the essential nature: flooded with the nectar of Shiva, it is knowledge abiding in light, beyond the midst of being, nonbeing, and the like.

[tal-a01-v85] Abiding in one's own place should be understood as being the seer, free of covering, purified by the pure insight that reveals the distinct reality.

[tal-a01-v86] When the functioning of the group-nature is understood, everything is accomplished; abandoning the lower and entering the higher, one becomes established in delight in the middle region.

[tal-a01-v87] Movement and rest, dream and waking, opening and closing, running and leaping, effort, and the feeling of power are all included.

[tal-a01-v88] The divisions of intellect, states, designations, and manifold actions are all pervaded here by that delight, which is Shiva, the supreme cause.

[tal-a01-v89] One whose mind is worn down by impurity can, through the mere restraint of memory, meditate on the supreme object of meditation that is present within the state of going and coming.

[tal-a01-v90] One reaches the supreme Shiva, called Bhairava, even through repetition; but true repetition is of that very nature, having fallen away from the states of being and nonbeing.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-mahāmantreśamantreśamantrāḥ śivapurogamāḥ / akalau sakalaśceti śivasyaiva vibhūtayaḥ tattvagrāmasya sarvasya dharmaḥ syādanapāyavān / ātmaiva hi svabhāvātmetyuktaṃ śrītriśiromate hṛdisthaṃ sarvadehasthaṃ svabhāvasthaṃ susūkṣmakam / sāmūhyaṃ caiva tattvānāṃ grāmaśabdena kīrtitam ātmaiva dharma ityuktaḥ śivāmṛtapariplutaḥ / prakāśāvasthitaṃ jñānaṃ bhāvābhāvādimadhyataḥ svasthāne vartanaṃ jñeyaṃ draṣṭṛtvaṃ vigatāvṛti / viviktavastukathitaśuddhavijñānanirmalaḥ grāmadharmavṛttiruktastasya sarvaṃ prasiddhyati / ūrdhva tyaktvādho viśetsa rāmastho madhyadeśagaḥ gatiḥ sthānaṃ svapnajāgradunmeṣaṇanimeṣaṇe / dhāvanaṃ plavanaṃ caiva āyāsaḥ śaktivedanam buddhibhedāstathā bhāvāḥ saṃjñāḥ karmāṇyanekaśaḥ / eṣa rāmo vyāpako@tra śivaḥ paramakāraṇam kalmaṣakṣīṇamanasā smṛtimātranirodhanāt / dhyāyate paramaṃ dhyeyaṃ gamāgamapade sthitam paraṃ śivaṃ tu vrajati bhairavākhyaṃ japādapi / tatsvarūpaṃ japaḥ prokto bhāvābhāvapadacyutaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v100] The lord of that group, greatly terrifying because he shatters the activity of worldly existence, is praised in the scripture by the teachers as Bhairava through these etymological meanings.

[tal-a01-v91] Even here, distinctions such as far and near are fashioned by his freedom and arise in dependence on the freedom of consciousness.

[tal-a01-v92] Thus, because he is full of freedom and able to accomplish even the most difficult deeds, in what form indeed does the supreme Lord not shine?

[tal-a01-v93] He shines uncovered, he shines with his own nature veiled, and he shines as both veiled and unveiled in many ways through association with difference.

[tal-a01-v94] Thus the triad of powers in the Lord, which is another name for his freedom, has been made manifest by the teachers under names such as will and the rest.

[tal-a01-v95] The Lord is taught through meaningful scriptural words as this great Bhairava, the supreme Lord, Pati, and Shiva.

[tal-a01-v96] He bears the universe by filling and sustaining it, he is resorted to with reflective awareness, he is of the nature of sound, and he brings good to those who fear samsara.

[tal-a01-v97] Even from a trembling touch born of fear of worldly existence, a reflective awareness of the fear of becoming can arise in the heart and become manifest through the descent of power.

[tal-a01-v98] He becomes manifest in those who dry up the time principle that drives the stars, and in those whose minds delight in absorption in the devouring of time.

[tal-a01-v99] Their roaring is for the fear of contracted bound beings—the roaring of the goddesses of one's own senses and also of the fourfold group of khecarī and others, within and without.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tadatrāpi tadīyena svātantryeṇopakalpitaḥ / dūrāsannādiko bhedaścitsvātantryavyapekṣayā evaṃ svātantryapūrṇatvādatidurghaṭakāryayam / kena nāma na rūpeṇa bhāsate parameśvaraḥ nirāvaraṇamābhāti bhātyābṛtanijātmakaḥ / āvṛtānāvṛto bhāti bahudhā bhedasaṃgamāt iti śaktitrayaṃ nāthe svātantryāparanāmakam / icchādibhirabhikhyābhirgurubhiḥ prakaṭīkṛtam devo hyanvarthaśāstroktaiḥ śabdaiḥ samupadiśyate / mahābhairavadevo@yaṃ patiryaḥ paramaḥ śivaḥ viśvaṃ bibharti pūraṇadhāraṇayogena tena ca śriyate / savimarśatayā rava rūpataśca saṃsārabhīruhitakṛcca saṃsārabhītijanitādravātparāmarśato@pi hṛdi jātaḥ / prakaṭībhūtaṃ bhavabhayavimarśanaṃ śaktipātato yena nakṣatraprerakakālatattvasaṃśoṣakāriṇo ye ca / kālagrāsasamādhānarasikamanaḥsu teṣu ca prakaṭaḥ saṃkocipaśujanabhiye yāsāṃ ravaṇaṃ svakaraṇadevīnām / antarbahiścaturvidhakhecaryādikagaṇasyāpi tasya svāmī saṃsāravṛttivighaṭanamahābhīmaḥ / bhairava iti gurubhirimairanvarthaiḥ saṃstutaḥ śāstre

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v101] Where there is no talk of what is to be rejected or accepted, there is play as the overflowing mass of one's own bliss, the will to abide in supremacy over all, and likewise autonomy.

[tal-a01-v102] Even in the undivided self, activity appears through difference as articulate expression; and because all manifestation illumines him, everything becomes his praise.

[tal-a01-v103] From the attainment of selfhood onward, in everything that is to be done, the course becomes inclined toward him—consisting of awareness, made of all action, and endowed with the powers of knowing and doing.

[tal-a01-v104] Thus, by etymological explanations in the scripture whose body is Śiva, the teachers remember the deity; because he teaches, restrains, protects, and matures, he benefits all. Therefore he is the Lord, Śiva himself consisting of the highest good, and there is nothing there that is not Śiva.

[tal-a01-v105] Since such a form may shine even to some extent in Rudra, Upendra, and others, the qualifier 'supreme and great state' is assumed for the one who removes limitation.

[tal-a01-v106] Thus, that true principle to be known is shown by me, by the command of Śiva, through one's own awareness, sound reasoning, the Lord's scripture, and the sequence of the Trika.

[tal-a01-v107] His three powers, beginning with parā, shine in emission, maintenance, resorption, and the fourth; therefore these are declared as twelve.

[tal-a01-v108] This one, of such full nature, is called the supreme Śiva; therefore worshippers are directly and fully established right there.

[tal-a01-v109] Even the arrangement of their divisions, parts, deficiencies, excesses, and so on is set forth in the scriptures solely by the force of his autonomy.

[tal-a01-v110] He is the single hero, then the paired one, having three powers and a fourfold nature, having five forms, this one with a sixfold nature, adorned as sevenfold and eightfold.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-heyopādeyakathāvirahe svānandaghanatayocchalanam / krīḍā sarvotkarṣeṇavartanecchā tathā svatantratvam vyavaharaṇamabhinne@pi svātmani bhedena saṃjalpaḥ / nikhilāvabhāsanācca dyotanamasya stutiryataḥ sakalam tatpravaṇamātmalābhātprabhṛti samaste@pi kartavye / bodhātmakaḥ samastakriyāmayo dṛkkriyāguṇaśca gatiḥ iti nirvacanaiḥ śivatanuśāstre gurubhiḥ smṛto devaḥ / śāsanarodhanapālanapācanayogātsa sarvamupakurute / tena patiḥ śreyomaya eva śivo nāśivaṃ kimapi tatra īdṛgrūpaṃ kiyadapi rudropendrādiṣu sphuredyena / tenāvacchedanude paramamahatpadaviśeṣaṇamupāttam iti yajjñeyasatattvaṃ darśyate tacchivājñayā / mayā svasaṃvitsattarkapatiśāstratrikakramāt tasya śaktaya evaitāstisro bhānti parādikāḥ / sṛṣṭau sthitau laye turye tenaitā dvādaśoditāḥ tāvānpūrṇasvabhāvo@sau paramaḥ śiva ucyate / tenātropāsakāḥ sākṣāttatraiva pariniṣṭhitāḥ tāsāmapi ca bhedāṃśanyūnādhikyādiyojanam / tatsvātantryabalādeva śāstreṣu paribhāṣitam ekavīro yāmalo@tha triśaktiścaturātmakaḥ / pañcamūrtiḥ ṣaḍātmāyaṃ saptako@ṣṭakabhūṣitaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v111] He has a ninefold nature, the power of the ten directions, and an elevenfold nature; thus Bhairava is the lord of the great twelve-spoked wheel.

[tal-a01-v112] Thus, in the wheel of the universe—whether thousand-spoked or even uncountably spoked—the Lord, the great sovereign whose power is the universe, expands.

[tal-a01-v113] Even among those wheels, the differences belonging to each wheel are explained, case by case, through a unity that follows the nature of its own group.

[tal-a01-v114] In the Traiśirasa doctrine, by the reckoning of four, six, two, and two, the Lord—whose own form is wondrous—is said to have sovereignty over six wheels.

[tal-a01-v115] There, the names of the goddesses of the wheel are determined according to differences of function and by etymological conception of the yoginīs associated with gentle or fierce forms and meditations.

[tal-a01-v116] For the one lord of consciousness, the inner body is indeed creative intuition; as gentle or in another measured form, the wheel of waves of consciousness is worshipped.

[tal-a01-v117] With the intention, 'May this be nourished,' the goddess-consciousness is nourished by such meditation mixed with articulate expression, and also by external activity.

[tal-a01-v118] When it becomes clear, it shines and grants him a corresponding fruit. Nourishment is like a dry place becoming a lake; therefore there is clear water.

[tal-a01-v119] Then, having followed that, meditation centered on it is extended; and there are phonemes which by their own nature flow with essence, as follows.

[tal-a01-v120] Those phonemes, mostly dental, labial, and dental, formed together with certain other sounds, attain the state of a seed and make that consciousness clear.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-navātmā daśadikchaktirekādaśakalātmakaḥ / dvādaśāramahācakranāyako bhairavastviti evaṃ yāvatsahasrāre niḥsaṃkhyāre@pi vā prabhuḥ / viśvacakre maheśāno viśvaśaktirvijṛmbhate teṣāmapi ca cakrāṇā svavargānugamātmanā / aikyena cakrago bhedastatra tatra nirūpitaḥ catuṣṣaḍdvirdvigaṇanāyogāttraiśirase mate / ṣaṭcakreśvaratā nāthasyoktā citranijākṛteḥ nāmāni cakradevīnāṃ tatra kṛtyavibhedataḥ / saumyaraudrākṛtidhyānayogīnyanvarthakalpanāt ekasya saṃvinnāthasya hyāntarī pratibhā tanuḥ / saumyaṃ vānyanmitaṃ saṃvidūrmicakramupāsyate asya syātpuṣṭirityeṣā saṃviddevī tathoditāt / dhyānātsaṃjalpasaṃmiśrād vyāpārāccāpi bāhyataḥ sphuṭībhūtā satī bhāti tasya tādṛkphalapradā / puṣṭiḥ śuṣkasya sarasībhāvo jalamataḥ sitam anugamya tato dhyānaṃ tatpradhānaṃ pratanyate / ye ca svabhāvato varṇā rasaniḥṣyandino yathā dantyauṣṭhyadantyaprāyāste kaiścidvarṇaiḥ kṛtāḥ saha / taṃ bījabhāvamāgatya saṃvidaṃ sphuṭayanti tām

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v121] Even thought-natured speech would not fill that very nourishment.

[tal-a01-v122] This is nectar, this is milk, ghee brings strength; by that nourish his seed and fill the action.

[tal-a01-v123] Therefore world-lord knowledge-Bhairava is worshipped by people desiring enjoyment and liberation, through limited and unlimited means.

[tal-a01-v124] Therefore the teacher instructed: those who know something apart from knowledge as sacrificial are even devotees of other deities.

[tal-a01-v125] They too, distinguishing the knowable, think through non-difference from knowledge, by the nature of unbroken I-awareness manifestation.

[tal-a01-v126] For the self-manifest there is no injunction prior; indeed deity-creation has arisen from power-cause.

[tal-a01-v127] But awareness is eternal and self-manifest in I-form; injunction is three-part command, and meditation is injunction-nature.

[tal-a01-v128] Indra and other deities are accomplished through injunction, but I-knowledge is not so; they take knowable form.

[tal-a01-v129] Seeing him only submerged, even knowing, they do not know; as said, they do not know me truly, therefore they wander.

[tal-a01-v130] But wandering is only attainment of limited form, as in 'gods and sacrificers go,' and by that it was described.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-puṣṭiṃ kuru rasenainamāpyāyaya tarāmiti / saṃjalpo@pi vikalpātmā kiṃ tāmeva na pūrayet amṛteyamidaṃ kṣīramidaṃ sarpirbalāvaham / tenāsya bījaṃ puṣṇīyāmityenāṃ pūrayetkriyām tasmādviśveśvaro bodhabhairavaḥ samupāsyate / avacchedānavacchidbhyāṃ bhogamokṣārthibhirjanaiḥ ye@pyanyadevatābhaktā ityato gururādiśat / ye bodhādvyatiriktaṃ hi kiṃcidyājyatayā viduḥ te@pi vedyaṃ viviñcānā bodhābhedena manvate / tenāvicchinnatāmarśarūpāhantāprathātmanaḥ svayaṃ-prathasya na vidhiḥ sṛṣṭyātmāsya ca pūrvagaḥ / vedyā hi devatāsṛṣṭiḥ śakterhetoḥ samutthitā ahaṃrūpā tu saṃvittirnityā svaprathanātmikā / vidhirniyogastryaṃśā ca bhāvanā codanātmikā tadekasiddhā indrādyā vidhipūrvā hi devatāḥ / ahaṃbodhastu na tathā te tu saṃvedyarūpatām unmagnāmeva paśyantastaṃ vidanto@pi no viduḥ / taduktaṃ na vidurmāṃ tu tattvenātaścalanti te calanaṃ tu vyavacchinnarūpatāpattireva yā / devāndevayajo yāntītyādi tena nyarūpyata

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v131] Those who, immersing knowability, know the consciousness-filled state there—even those devotees go to me, the unlimited.

[tal-a01-v132] Everywhere here the word I denotes awareness only; it is indicated by enjoyer and lord words as sacrificial-sacrificer status.

[tal-a01-v133] Sacrificer-ship is awareness only; the sacrificial is not other. No form is established as another deity.

[tal-a01-v134] Injunction is not said here, nor mantra or operation-abode; this self, covering itself, is situated and has gone to inert state.

[tal-a01-v135] But the covered-uncovered self reaches from gods to immobile; the duality of this inert and non-inert is a wonder.

[tal-a01-v137] By that, variety is situated in many ways in the uncovered portion of the non-inert part, named atom and so on.

[tal-a01-v138] In awareness-form there is no real difference, although fixed; yet it is perceived by degree of covering removal.

[tal-a01-v139] We will say that in detail in the determination of grace-descent; completing, otherness and grossness will be discussed.

[tal-a01-v140] Therefore the lord manifests toward some knower his own full form, by a sequence of partial aspects.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-nimajjya vedyatāṃ ye tu tatra saṃvinmayīṃ sthitim / viduste hyanavacchinnaṃ tadbhaktā api yānti mām sarvatrātra hyahaṃśabdo bodhamātraikavācakaḥ / sa bhoktṛprabhuśabdābhyāṃ yājyayaṣṭṭatayoditaḥ yājamānī saṃvideva yājyā nānyeti coditam / na tvākṛtiḥ kuto@pyanyā devatā na hi socitā vidhiśca noktaḥ ko@pyatra mantrādi vṛttidhāma vā / so@yamātmānamāvṛtya sthito jaḍapadaṃ gataḥ āvṛtānāvṛtātmā tu devādisthāvarāntagaḥ / jaḍājaḍasyāpyetasya dvairūpyasyāsti citratā tasya svatantrabhāvo hi kiṃ kiṃ yanna vicintayet / taduktaṃ triśiraḥśāstre saṃbuddha iti vetti yaḥ tenājaḍasya bhāgasya pudgalāṇvādisaṃjñinaḥ / anāvaraṇabhāgāṃśe vaicitryaṃ bahudhā sthitam saṃvidrūpe na bhedo@sti vāstavo yadyapi dhruve / tathāpyāvṛtinirhāsatāratamyātsa lakṣyate tadvistareṇa vakṣyāmaḥ śaktipātavinirṇaye / samāpya paratāṃ sthaulyaprasaṃge carcayiṣyate ataḥ kaṃcitpramātāraṃ prati prathayate vibhuḥ / pūrṇameva nijaṃ rūpaṃ kaṃcidaṃśāṃśikākramāt

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v141] Indeed, manifestation of world-nature as one self-form is supreme knowledge for atoms; other knowledge is inferior and much.

[tal-a01-v142] That, manifesting by direct means and by that means etc., differs here by various breaks.

[tal-a01-v143] There also, because self-other door-gate-ness is partial, greater difference arises by obstruction and non-obstruction.

[tal-a01-v144] The means of knowledge is not called ignorance; knowledge only is subtle, supreme, and of will-nature, according to opinion.

[tal-a01-v145] In knowledge, the distinction between means and goal is a coarse level. This very same thing is the power of action, which alone causes both bondage and liberation.

[tal-a01-v146] In the first mode, which is self-awareness resting in a single non-conceptual abode, whatever flashes forth clearly and directly is called will.

[tal-a01-v147] Just as an object can appear clearly to someone whose perception has flashed forth, even without any deliberate mental connection, so too for some people the state of being Śiva shines forth directly.

[tal-a01-v148] But when recognition does not come immediately, they call it the means of knowledge: through repeatedly working with conceptual elements in a steady sequence of certainty, one comes to reflective awareness.

[tal-a01-v149] But what is taught as the means of action works by accomplishing externalized objects shaped by conceptual thought. Because it remains within difference, it does not by itself lead to liberation.

[tal-a01-v150] For in the teaching of the revered scripture, there is no action separate from knowledge. Knowledge itself, when firmly established in that way, reaches the culmination of yoga.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-viśvabhāvaikabhāvātmasvarūpaprathanaṃ hi yat / aṇūnāṃ tatparaṃ jñānaṃ tadanyadaparaṃ bahu tacca sākṣādupāyena tadupāyādināpi ca / prathamānaṃ vicitrābhirbhaṃgībhiriha bhidyate tatrāpi svaparadvāradvāritvātsarvaśoṃśaśaḥ / vyavadhānāvyavadhinā bhūyānbhedaḥ pravartate jñānasya cābhyupāyo yo na tadajñānamucyate / jñānameva tu tatsūkṣmaṃ paraṃ tvicchātmakaṃ matam upāyopeyabhāvastu jñānasya sthaulyaviśramaḥ / eṣaiva ca kriyāśaktirbandhamokṣaikakāraṇam tatrādye svaparāmarśe nirvikalpaikadhāmani / yatsphuretprakaṭaṃ sākṣāttadicchākhyaṃ prakīrtitam yathā visphuritadṛśāmanusandhiṃ vināpyalam / bhāti bhāvaḥ sphuṭastadvatkeṣāmapi śivātmatā bhūyo bhūyo vikalpāṃśaniścayakramacarcanāt / yatparāmarśamabhyeti jñānopāyaṃ tu tadviduḥ yattu tatkalpanāklṛptabahirbhūtārthasādhanam / kriyopāyaṃ tadāmnātaṃ bhedo nātrāpavargagaḥ yato nānyā kriyā nāma jñānameva hi tattathā / rūḍheryogāntatāṃ prāptamiti śrīgamaśāsane

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v151] Yoga is not different from action, and action is not different from yoga. The cognition that is firmly grounded in reality and brings the impressions of one's own mind to rest is what is called action.

[tal-a01-v152] In one's own mind there are latent impressions born from karma, impurity, and maya. The cognition that arises to calm those impressions is essentially of the nature of consciousness itself.

[tal-a01-v153] That same cognition, which rests upon the outer range of principles that give rise to the body, is action. And that very same cognition becomes yoga when it dissolves those principles back into consciousness.

[tal-a01-v154] Even in everyday life, when one thinks 'I am going', there is first just an inner flash. That same flash enters the body, the place, and the senses, and then it becomes the act of going.

[tal-a01-v155] Therefore, even what is called action is really nothing but knowledge. For that reason, it is right to say that knowledge alone brings liberation, and this has already been stated.

[tal-a01-v156] Liberation is nothing other than the unfolding of one's own true nature. And the self's true nature is nothing other than consciousness. The verse then turns to what comes next.

[tal-a01-v157] The powers of action and the rest are grounded in the nature of consciousness, because they cannot belong to anything unconscious, and no separate substrate for them can be established.

[tal-a01-v158] In the scripture of the Supreme Lord, the powers are not said to have any separate substrate, as if they were qualities in the manner taught by the followers of Kaṇāda.

[tal-a01-v159] If the powers of seeing, action, will, and so on were truly separate, then saying 'Shiva is one' would become mere words without any real basis.

[tal-a01-v160] For this reason, freedom is nothing but consciousness itself; and when examined closely, it is seen to unfold into many powers.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-yogo nānyaḥ kriyā nānyā tattvārūḍhā hi yā matiḥ / svacittavāsanāśāntau sā kriyetyabhidhīyate svacitte vāsanāḥ karmamalamāyāprasūtayaḥ / tāsāṃ śāntinimittaṃ yā matiḥ saṃvitsvabhāvikā sā dehārambhibāhyasthatattvabrātādhiśāyinī / kriyā saiva ca yogaḥ syāttattvānāṃ cillayīkṛtau loke@pi kila gacchāmītyevamantaḥ sphuraiva yā / sā dehaṃ deśamakṣāṃścāpyāviśantī gatikriyā tasmātkriyāpi yā nāma jñānameva hi sā tataḥ / jñānameva vimokṣāya yuktaṃ caitadudāhṛtam mokṣo hi nāma naivānyaḥ svarūpaprathanaṃ hi saḥ / svarūpaṃ cātmanaḥ saṃvinnānyattatra tu yāḥ punaḥ kriyādikāḥ śaktayastāḥ saṃvidrūpādhikā nahi / asaṃvidrūpatāyogāddharmiṇaścānirūpaṇāt parameśvaraśāstre hi na ca kāṇādadṛṣṭivat / śaktīnāṃ dharmarūpāṇāmāśrayaḥ ko@pi kathyate tataśca dṛkkriyecchādyā bhinnāścecchaktayastathā / ekaḥ śiva itīyaṃ vāgvastuśūnyaiva jāyate tasmātsaṃvittvamevaitatsvātantryaṃ yattadapyalam / vivicyamānaṃ bahvīṣu paryavasyati śaktiṣu

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v161] Since liberation is the self's own shining forth, there is no reason to think that merely knowing a cause and its effect will automatically bring liberation.

[tal-a01-v162] Although knowledge is sometimes described as the cause of liberation, that is not the primary way to understand their relation; so the objection raised earlier does not hold.

[tal-a01-v163] Action is by nature knowledge itself, but as it takes on a grosser form in the self, its variety becomes visible.

[tal-a01-v164] Within the path of action, the means are divided into inner and outer and then into many further kinds, so they become countless.

[tal-a01-v165] This also removes the doubt some wise people had, that because the means differ, liberation itself might differ.

[tal-a01-v166] Even if liberation comes about through different causes, such as the destruction of impurity and its power or the falling away of concealment, liberation itself is not different, just as the breaking of a pot is one kind of event though caused in different ways.

[tal-a01-v167] This threefold division was taught by the Supreme Lord in the scripture called Śrīpūrva, in the section that determines the nature of penetration.

[tal-a01-v168] When a person who is thinking of nothing at all is awakened by the teacher and penetration arises, that is called the śāmbhava penetration.

[tal-a01-v169] When one contemplates a reality without utterance, using the mind alone, and attains penetration in that way, it is called the śākta penetration.

[tal-a01-v170] The penetration that arises through utterance, bodily practice, meditation, letters, and imagined locations is properly called the āṇava penetration.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-yataścātmaprathā mokṣastannehāśaṅkyamīdṛśam / nāvaśyaṃ kāraṇātkārya tajjñānyapi na mucyate yato jñānena mokṣasya yā hetuphalatoditā / na sā mukhyā tato nāyaṃ prasaṃga iti niścitam evaṃ jñānasvabhāvaiva kriyā sthūlatvamātmani / yato vahati tenāsyāṃ citratā dṛśyatāṃ kila kriyopāye@bhyupāyānāṃ grāhyabāhyavibhedinām / bhedopabhedavaividhyānniḥsaṃkhyatvamavāntarāt anena caitatpradhvastaṃ yatkecana śaśaṅkire / upāyabhedānmokṣe@pi bhedaḥ syāditi sūrayaḥ malatacchaktividhvaṃsatirobhūcyutimadhyataḥ / hetubhede@pi no bhinnā ghaṭadhvaṃsādivṛttivat tadetattrividhatvaṃ hi śāstre śrīpūrvanāmani / ādeśi parameśitrā samāveśavinirṇaye akiṃciccintakasyaiva guruṇā pratibodhataḥ / utpadyate ya āveśaḥ śāmbhavo@sāvidīritaḥ uccārarahitaṃ vastu cetasaiva vicintayan / yaṃ samāveśamāpnoti śāktaḥ so@trābhidhīyate uccārakaraṇadhyānavarṇasthānaprakalpanaiḥ / yo bhavetsa samāveśaḥ samyagāṇava ucyate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v171] The expression 'one who thinks of nothing' means that conceptual construction is not in use, and through that there is a sudden absorption into what is to be known.

[tal-a01-v172] How does that happen? It happens through a most weighty teacher, whose awareness is turned toward the knowable and whose awakening is immediately mature.

[tal-a01-v173] The verse gives a grammatical explanation of the earlier expression and adds that, for the dependent self, penetration means sinking into its own true form.

[tal-a01-v174] The meaning here is that one comes to share the nature of Shambhu, the primal Lord who is never separate from his power; this meaning is to be understood as shining forth on its own.

[tal-a01-v175] Even without any determinate judgment, it suddenly appears reflected in the mirror of the subject, overwhelms the subject, and displays its own majesty.

[tal-a01-v176] Depending on the degree of purity of the heart, the knowable appears in two ways: as mere consciousness, or as something inert and constructed.

[tal-a01-v177] The other kind of knowable is also treated as real in its own way; penetration into what is inert takes the form of a reflected image.

[tal-a01-v178] Penetration into consciousness is nothing other than identity with it; for that reason the awareness involved is non-conceptual and does not depend on contemplation or similar practices.

[tal-a01-v179] Here śāmbhava penetration is the attainment of identity with Shiva; any determinate understandings that arise afterward come by its grace, not as its cause.

[tal-a01-v180] Even if later determinate understandings arise in harmony with that identity, they cannot be its means, because they depend on conceptual construction, while the valid cognition in question is non-conceptual.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-akiṃciccintakasyeti vikalpānupayogitā / tayā ca jhaṭiti jñeyasamāpattirnirūpyate sā kathaṃ bhavatītyāha guruṇātigarīyasā / jñeyābhimukhabodhena drākprarūḍhatvaśālinā tṛtīyārthe tasi vyākhyā vā vaiyadhikaraṇyataḥ / āveśaścāsvatantrasya svatadrūpanimajjanāt paratadrūpatā śambhorādyācchaktyavibhāginaḥ / tenāyamatra vākyārtho vijñeyaṃ pronmiṣatsvayam vināpi niścayena drāk mātṛdarpaṇabimbitam / mātāramadharīkurvat svāṃ vibhūtiṃ pradarśayat āste hṛdayanairmalyātiśaye tāratamyataḥ / jñeyaṃ dvidhā ca cinmātraṃ jaḍaṃ cādyaṃ ca kalpitam itarattu tathā satyaṃ tadvibhāgo@yamīdṛśaḥ / jaḍena yaḥ samāveśaḥ sapraticchandakākṛtiḥ caitanyena samāveśastādātmyaṃ nāparaṃ kila / tenāvikalpā saṃvittirbhāvanādyanapekṣiṇī śivatādātmyamāpannā samāveśo@tra śāṃbhavaḥ / tatprasādātpunaḥ paścādbhāvino@tra viniścayāḥ santu tādātmyamāpannā na tu teṣāmupāyatā / vikalpāpekṣayā mānamavikalpamiti bruvan

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v181] This has already been answered, for what has been grasped is then followed by conceptual thought. Determinate cognition shines forth very clearly, so the objection does not stand.

[tal-a01-v182] By the force of unity with the nonconceptual sense of I grasp, the object is apprehended. In nonconceptual self-awareness, it is simply the flashing forth of the object that is known.

[tal-a01-v183] That flashing forth is not established by conceptual thought, since conceptual thought does not directly depend on the object. It belongs only to awareness, which rests in its own clarity or lack of clarity.

[tal-a01-v184] Both independence from and dependence on conceptual thought can occur in the same self. For example, even at night a jewel expert may see gems revealed only for the brief moment of a lightning flash.

[tal-a01-v185] He can discern the particular features of many jewels. If awareness is clear, this happens through the force of prior practice.

[tal-a01-v186] This will be discussed later as arising from the will of the unrestricted Lord. The immersion has been described as having fifty forms.

[tal-a01-v187] This division is based on the clear distinctions within the thirty-six principles. Among them is a triad made of self, knowledge, and power.

[tal-a01-v188] In order, the triad called self, knowledge, and power is divided into four, ten, and three forms. This is because that triad is all-pervading.

[tal-a01-v189] So this triad is counted in distinction from the nonpervading principles. It also stands in mutual relation through impurity, the process of purification, and purity.

[tal-a01-v190] The elements are established by direct perception and can also be inferred from cause and effect. For that reason they are treated as separate from the group of principles.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-pratyukta eva siddhaṃ hi vikalpenānugamyate / gṛhītamiti suspaṣṭā niścayasya yataḥ prathā gṛhṇāmītyavikalpaikyabalāttu pratipadyate / avikalpātmasaṃvittau yā sphurattaiva vastunaḥ sā siddhirna vikalpāttu vastvapekṣāvivarjitāt / kevalaṃ saṃvidaḥ so@yaṃ nairmalyetaraviśramaḥ yadvikalpānapekṣatvasāpekṣatve nijātmani / niśīthe@pi maṇijñānī vidyutkālapradarśitān tāṃstānviśeṣāṃścinute ratnānāṃ bhūyasāmapi / nairmalyaṃ saṃvidaścedaṃ pūrvābhyāsavaśādatho aniyantreśvarecchāta ityetaccarcayiṣyate / pañcāśadvidhatā cāsya samāveśasya varṇitā tattvaṣaṭtriṃśakaitatsthasphuṭabhedābhisandhitaḥ / etattattvāntare yatpuṃvidyāśaktyātmakaṃ trayam ambhodhikāṣṭhājvalanasaṃkhyairbhedairyataḥ kramāt / puṃvidyāśaktisaṃjñaṃ yattatsarvavyāpakaṃ yataḥ avyāpakebhyastenedaṃ bhedena gaṇitaṃ kila / aśuddhiśuddhyamānatvaśuddhitastu mitho@pi tat bhūtānyadhyakṣasiddhāni kāryahetvanumeyataḥ / tattvavargātpṛthagbhūtasamākhyānyata eva hi

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v191] The elements are within the range of all cognition, so the knowers place them in the fourfold scheme. There they find the proper room for their abiding.

[tal-a01-v192] The immersion of Rudra's power is said to be fivefold. But then what room would there be for it in the description of elemental immersion and the other forms?

[tal-a01-v193] If one objects that such absorption can arise by contextual association, that is possible; but it is not for us, because people have different tastes and this absorption excludes the ordinary mind.

[tal-a01-v194] It is said that in dualistic teachings the elements and so on are regarded as separated from the supreme Lord, but in this teaching, which is free from duality, it is not so.

[tal-a01-v195] All that is the thirty-sixfold reality, and whatever else there may be, all of that is the great Goddess, the unobstructed power of Rudra.

[tal-a01-v196] For that very reason, in the second section the universal nature of earth and the other realities was expounded through divisions such as the fifteenfold scheme.

[tal-a01-v197] Therefore, just as in the earlier discussion awareness of the partless reality was understood through aspects such as qualities, parts, and wholes, so too it should be understood here.

[tal-a01-v198] Therefore, through properties such as nonconceptuality, firmness, and majesty, or through other properties that are inherent power-forms, the reality can be approached.

[tal-a01-v199] Thus, those whose mental impressions arise from streams of concepts awakened by scripture worship that all-pervading supreme Lord, either wholly or in part.

[tal-a01-v200] Through their skill in the properties that shine within their own concepts, they come to rest upon the bearer of those properties as non-different and filled with the fullness of all properties.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-sarvapratītisadbhāvagocaraṃ bhūtameva hi / viduścatuṣṭaye cātra sāvakāśe tadāsthitim rudraśaktisamāveśaḥ pañcadhā nanu carcyate / ko@vakāśo bhavettatra bhautāveśādivarṇane prasaṃgādetaditicetsamādhiḥ saṃbhavannayam / nāsmākaṃ mānasāvarjī loko bhinnaruciryataḥ ucyate dvaitaśāstreṣu parameśādvibheditā / bhūtādīnāṃ yathā sātra na tathā dvayavarjite yāvānṣaṭtriṃśakaḥ so@yaṃ yadanyadapi kiṃcana / etāvatī mahādevī rudraśaktiranargalā tata eva dvitīye@sminnadhikāre nyarūpyata / dharāderviśvarūpatvaṃ pāñcadaśyādibhedataḥ tasmādyathā purasthe@rthe guṇādyaṃśāṃśikāmukhāt / niraṃśabhāvasaṃbodhastathaivātrāpi budhyatām ata evāvikalpatvadhrauvyaprābhavavaibhavaiḥ / anyairvā śaktirūpatvāddharmaiḥ svasamavāyibhiḥ sarvaśo@pyatha vāṃśena taṃ vibhuṃ parameśvaram / upāsate vikalpaughasaṃskārādye śrutotthitāt te tattatsvavikalpāntaḥsphurattaddharmapāṭavāt / dharmiṇaṃ pūrṇadharmaughamabhedenādhiśerate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v201] For this reason the lord of Śrīvidyā respectfully said: if conceptual construction did not make your nonconceptual nature an object for sense-born cognition, then clear experiences with varied images inscribed within would not arise.

[tal-a01-v202] This is stated in the Śrīmataṅga and other texts, where the abode of the Lord is described, with various qualifications, as consisting of the rays of his own power.

[tal-a01-v203] In that divine light there is a brilliantly radiant, motionless presence with an unmoving form; that alone is the supreme, subtle culmination, whose nature is nectar in all directions.

[tal-a01-v204] With all coverings destroyed, peaceful, intent on reality alone, free from beginning and end, and pure, that state is nevertheless spoken of figuratively as having a form.

[tal-a01-v205] This figurative way of speaking has a clear reason and purpose: through it clarity quickly arises in the qualified subject, and that leads to abiding in full absorption in that reality.

[tal-a01-v206] Those very qualities, called powers, are worshipped in various fitting forms so that one may become fully absorbed in that reality.

[tal-a01-v207] In that context, an unlimited power or even limited powers may be drawn in, according to the principle by which what is invoked becomes present, and according to nearness or distance.

[tal-a01-v208] Because of its pervasiveness, that reality draws in all powers, along with fullness, luminosity, the nature of consciousness, and the state of being Bhairava.

[tal-a01-v209] Sadashiva and the other principles below the highest, lacking full upward pervasion, can draw in powers only to the extent that their worship is near or far.

[tal-a01-v210] In this condition, the path taught here is called the Shakta path: it is a conceptual course, because it works through distinctions and their counterparts.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-ūcivānata eva śrīvidyādhipatirādarāt / tvatsvarūpamavikalpamakṣajā kalpane na viṣayīkaroti cet / antarullikhitacitrasaṃvido no bhaveyuranubhūtayaḥ sphuṭāḥ taduktaṃ śrīmataṅgādau svaśaktikiraṇātmakam / atha patyuradhiṣṭhānamityādyuktaṃ viśeṣaṇaiḥ tasyāṃ divi sudīptātmā niṣkampo@calamūrtimān / kāṣṭhā saiva parā sūkṣmā sarvadikkāmṛtātmikā pradhvastāvaraṇā śāntā vastumātrātilālasā / ādyantoparatā sādhvī mūrtitvenopacaryate tathopacārasyātraitannimitaṃ saprayojanam / tanmukhā sphuṭatā dharmiṇyāśu tanmayatāsthitiḥ ta eva dharmāḥ śaktyākhyāstaistairucitarūpakaiḥ / ākāraiḥ paryupāsyante tanmayībhāvasiddhaye tatra kācitpunaḥ śaktiranantā vā mitāśca vā / ākṣipeddhavatāsattvanyāyāddūrāntikatvataḥ tena pūrṇasvabhāvatvaṃ prakāśatvaṃ cidātmatā / bhairavatvaṃ viśvaśaktīrākṣipedvyāpakatvataḥ sadāśivādayastūrdhvavyāptyabhāvādadhojuṣaḥ / śaktīḥ samākṣipeyustadupāsāntikadūrataḥ itthaṃ-bhāve ca śāktākhyo vaikalpikapathakramaḥ / iha tūkto yatastasmāt pratiyogyavikalpakam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v211] One who is established in the nonconceptual path, by whatever route they enter—from the earth principle up to Sadashiva—through that very route becomes Shiva.

[tal-a01-v212] In a pure heart, illumined by the first flash of that level, awareness comes to recognize itself as supreme Shiva through that very opening.

[tal-a01-v213] Thus, those who live close to the wise teacher know this good means, which partakes of supreme will-power, as the Shambhava immersion.

[tal-a01-v214] Now the Shakta mode is described: it works clearly through mind, intellect, thought, and ego-making, in a conceptual way, dealing with things like will that are, in reality, made of maya.

[tal-a01-v215] The Shakta mode works through identification and through the sequence of intention and determination; even though it is a means based in maya, at its end it becomes nonconceptual.

[tal-a01-v216] The nonconceptual state that appears in a bound soul is indeed called Shambhava, but it is incomplete because of the defect of the limited knower; when that defect falls away, it blossoms fully.

[tal-a01-v217] Thus, in the Shakta mode there is a conceptual level marked by the awareness of agency; even when that awareness is clear, it still involves contraction, as explained earlier.

[tal-a01-v218] Likewise, for one who is intent on dissolving the whole mass of contraction, that power becomes radiant and can bring about the inner appearance of whatever is desired.

[tal-a01-v219] One might ask whether conceptual cognition exists in the Anava means. The answer is that, as defined here, the Anava means is marked by the absence of utterance, so that kind of conceptual operation belongs to another means.

[tal-a01-v220] Here the word utterance covers outward expression and related operations. These are not what define the Shakta means, because the Shakta means is characterized by the play of difference and nondifference, which is the very nature of power.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-avikalpapathārūḍho yena yena pathā viśet / dharāsadāśivāntena tena tena śivībhavet nirmale hṛdaye prāgryasphuradbhūmyaṃśabhāsini / prakāśe tanmukhenaiva saṃvitparaśivātmatā evaṃ parecchāśaktyaṃśasadupāyamimaṃ viduḥ / śāmbhavākhyaṃ samāveśaṃ sumatyantenivāsinaḥ śākto@tha bhaṇyate cetodhī-manohaṃkṛti sphuṭam / savikalpatayā māyāmayamicchādi vastutaḥ abhimānena saṃkalpādhyavasāyakrameṇa yaḥ / śāktaḥ sa māyopāyo@pi tadante nirvikalpakaḥ paśorvai yāvikalpā bhūrdaśā sā śāmbhavī param / apūrṇā mātṛdaurātmyāttadapāye vikasvarā evaṃ vaikalpikī bhūmiḥ śākte kartṛtvavedane / yasyāṃ sphuṭe paraṃ tvasyāṃ saṃkocaḥ pūrvanītitaḥ tathā saṃkocasaṃbhāravilāyanaparasya tu / sā yatheṣṭāntarābhāsakāriṇī śaktirujjvalā nanu vaikalpikī kiṃ dhīrāṇave nāsti tatra sā / anyopāyātra tūccārarahitatvaṃ nyarūpayat uccāraśabdenātroktā bahvantena tadādayaḥ / śaktyupāye na santyete bhedābhedau hi śaktitā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v221] The limited self is defined by clear difference, and the Anava means based on that works through conceptual thought and determination; yet at its culmination it becomes nonconceptual.

[tal-a01-v222] An objection arises: how could intellect, mind, ego, and the individual self pervade Shiva, since they exist below him? How, then, can such a teaching be stated?

[tal-a01-v223] The answer is that, in reality, it is Shiva alone. Being self-luminous, he conceals his own nature and then appears again in that very form.

[tal-a01-v224] Even in dualistic scriptures such as the Matanga, this is clearly explained: the light that appears in the lower levels is the established manifestation of Shiva himself, who pervades downward.

[tal-a01-v225] For this reason, the supreme state shines even on the level of intellect and mind.

[tal-a01-v226] Both of these immersions indeed move toward the ocean of the nonconceptual, but without firm establishment in that state, nothing at all is accomplished.

[tal-a01-v227] One should not assume any difference in the fruit of awareness here; rather, it was indicated that conceptual construction has a primary role in this context.

[tal-a01-v228] Even in the view that makes validity depend on conceptual construction, the nonconceptual is still valid—but its validity is reached through the ordered sequence of those very concepts.

[tal-a01-v229] One who does not know the truth of the jewel may first practice through the means of certainty; by attaining the meansless, non-conceptual state, that person is called a knower of the jewel.

[tal-a01-v230] Here the means of non-difference is called śāmbhava, the means of both difference and non-difference is called śākta, and the means of difference is called āṇava.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-aṇurnāma sphuṭo bhedastadupāya ihāṇavaḥ / vikalpaniścayātmaiva paryante nirvikalpakaḥ nanu dhī-mānasāhaṃkṛtpumāṃso vyāpnuyuḥ śivam / nādhovartitayā tena kathitaṃ kathamīdṛśam ucyate vastuto@smākaṃ śiva eva tathāvidhaḥ / svarūpagopanaṃ kṛtvā svaprakāśaḥ punastathā dvaitaśāstre mataṅgādau cāpyetatsunirūpitam / adhovyāptuḥ śivasyaiva sa prakāśo vyavasthitaḥ yena buddhi-manobhūmāvapi bhāti paraṃ padam dvāvapyetau samāveśau nirvikalpārṇavaṃ prati / prayāta eva tadrūḍhiṃ vinā naiva hi kiṃcana saṃvittiphalabhiccātra na prakalpyetyato@bravīt / kalpanāyāśca mukhyatvamatraiva kila sūcitam vikalpāpekṣayā yo@pi prāmāṇyaṃ prāha tanmate / tadvikalpakramopāttanirvikalpapramāṇatā ratnatattvamavidvānprāṅniścayopāyacarcanāt / anupāyāvikalpāptau ratnajña iti bhaṇyate abhedopāyamatroktaṃ śāmbhavaṃ śāktamucyate / bhedābhedātmakopāyaṃ bhedopāyaṃ tadāṇavam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v231] In the end, within knowledge accompanied by means, the entire expanse of action will be included in a very clear form.

[tal-a01-v232] Action is not something other than knowledge; it is knowledge that has taken on a sequential form through the force of means, and this was stated earlier as action.

[tal-a01-v233] Right knowledge, abiding in both self and other, is the sole cause of liberation, because the divisions of self, other, and so on are nothing more than constructions.

[tal-a01-v234] Even when all things are equally constructed, a teacher whose nature is the flashing forth of unity is called one-natured, accomplished, and liberated.

[tal-a01-v235] As far as that continuum extends, it is declared to be the teacher; and because it is made of right knowledge, one is liberated by one's own self through it.

[tal-a01-v236] For that very reason the knower carries his own continuum across; this is well established by reason and scripture, because to that extent the sage is one.

[tal-a01-v237] Therefore some object here: if liberation comes from knowledge, how could initiation and other ritual actions bring about liberation?

[tal-a01-v238] If action is of the nature of knowledge, the objectors ask whether knowledge liberates only where it is located and what happens in liberating another; but they are dismissed at the root, and the text turns to what others have established.

[tal-a01-v239] Some say impurity is a substance, like a film over the eye, and initiation is the action that removes it, like applying collyrium.

[tal-a01-v240] We will refute that view later, since it is condemned by reason and scripture, and we will also show the true status of impurity, māyā, and karma.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-ante jñāne@tra sopāye samastaḥ karmavistaraḥ / prasphuṭenaiva rūpeṇa bhāvī so@ntarbhaviṣyati kriyā hi nāma vijñānānnānyadvastu kramātmatām / upāyavaśataḥ prāptaṃ tatkriyeti puroditam samyagjñānaṃ ca muktyekakāraṇaṃ svaparasthitam / yato hi kalpanāmātraṃ svaparādivibhūtayaḥ tulye kālpanikatve ca yadaikyasphuraṇātmakaḥ / guruḥ sa tāvadekātmā siddho muktaśca bhaṇyate yāvānasya hi saṃtāno gurustāvatsa kīrtitaḥ / samyagjñānamayaśceti svātmanā mucyate tataḥ tata eva svasaṃtānaṃ jñānī tārayatītyadaḥ / yuktyāgamābhyāṃ saṃsiddhaṃ tāvāneko yato muniḥ tenātra ye codayanti nanu jñānādvimuktatā / dīkṣādikā kriyā ceyaṃ sā kathaṃ muktaye bhavet jñānātmā seti cejjñānaṃ yatrasthaṃ taṃ vimocayet / anyasya mocane vāpi bhavetkiṃ nāsamañjasam / iti te mūlataḥ kṣiptā yattvatrānyaiḥ samarthitam malo nāma kila dravyaṃ cakṣuḥsthapaṭalādivat / tadvihantrī kriyā dīkṣā tvañjanādikakarmavat tatpurastānniṣetsyāmo yuktyāgamavigarhitam / malamāyākarmaṇāṃ ca darśayiṣyāmahe sthitim

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v241] Thus, in the knowledge that operates through the means of the three powers, the last is the root, above it is the middle, and above that is the highest, first level.

[tal-a01-v242] Even beyond that is a supreme knowledge, free of means and the rest, resting in the power of bliss; here it is called the unsurpassed.

[tal-a01-v243] That self-luminous knowledge, whose true presence is rare even for the lords of knowledge and others, is spoken of in the revered Siddha Tantra.

[tal-a01-v244] This is also clearly indicated in the Mālinī, in the eighteenth chapter, by the statement that it is not attained without the grace of Śaṅkara.

[tal-a01-v245] By this very teaching in the Mālinīvijayottara, the fourfold knowledge that brings the great rise of accomplishment and liberation is systematized by me in this teaching called the Tantrāloka.

[tal-a01-v246] Here, whatever is reflected on, whether inwardly or outwardly, first shines forth with its form not yet unfolded.

[tal-a01-v247] That first manifestation appears with an unopened, indescribable form; doubt arises only when some form is determined, and not otherwise.

[tal-a01-v248] In the question 'what is this?', one part of the primary appearance is already well determined, while doubt remains because properties such as 'it is' or 'it is not' are not yet unfolded.

[tal-a01-v249] The word 'what' does not reveal any additional meaning; it simply denotes the thing itself while its form remains unopened.

[tal-a01-v250] The doubt 'is it a post or a person?' is not the primary kind of doubt; it is really the arising of determination among many possible properties.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-evaṃ śaktitrayopāyaṃ yajjñānaṃ tatra paścimam / mūlaṃ taduttaraṃ madhyamuttarottaramādimam tato@pi paramaṃ jñānamupāyādivivarjitam / ānandaśaktiviśrāntamanuttaramihocyate tatsvaprakāśaṃ vijñānaṃ vidyāvidyeśvarādibhiḥ / api durlabhasadbhāvaṃ śrīsiddhātantra ucyate mālinyāṃ sūcitaṃ caitatpaṭale@ṣṭādaśe sphuṭam / na caitadaprasannena śaṃkareṇeti vākyataḥ ityanenaiva pāṭhena mālinīvijayottare / iti jñānacatuṣkaṃ yatsiddhimuktimahodayam / tanmayā tantryate tantrālokanāmnyatra śāsane tatreha yadyadantarvā bahirvā parimṛśyate / anudghāṭitarūpaṃ tatpūrvameva prakāśate tathānudghāṭitākārā nirvācyenātmanā prathā / saṃśayaḥ kutracidrūpe niścite sati nānyathā etatkimiti mukhye@sminnetadaṃśaḥ suniścitaḥ / saṃśayo@stitvanāstyādidharmānudghāṭitātmakaḥ kimityetasya śabdasya nādhiko@rthaḥ prakāśate / kiṃ tvanunmudritākāraṃ vastvevābhidadhātyayam sthāṇurvā puruṣo veti na mukhyo@styeṣa saṃśayaḥ / bhūyaḥsthadharmajāteṣu niścayotpāda eva hi

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v251] Again, doubt arises in the 'what' aspect because two forms that could be reflected on remain unopened; conceptual construction, by contrast, is clearly different.

[tal-a01-v252] Therefore, the first manifestation of a being whose nature is not yet unfolded is here called indication, question, and indeed doubt.

[tal-a01-v253] As self-awareness expands along the path by which forms and beings that were not yet fully revealed come forth, it becomes the questioner and takes on the condition of the disciple.

[tal-a01-v254] Because the certainty of inner reflective awareness is then concealed, the questioner also partakes in the rise of withdrawal that comes immediately after expansion.

[tal-a01-v255] To whatever extent there is a clearly manifest outward expansion in which her own form has not yet fully opened, to that same extent she is called the questioner.

[tal-a01-v256] In this way, awakening itself takes the form of question and answer; so even in the roles of teacher and disciple, the difference of bodies is not ultimately real.

[tal-a01-v257] Because awareness is of the nature of awareness, it makes the many forms that abide within it appear outwardly, just as both the general and specific features of a grape are manifested.

[tal-a01-v258] When some property is projected only in a general way, while a further specific aspect is still awaited, that general projection has the nature of doubt.

[tal-a01-v259] When the awaited specific aspect finally settles, determination arises; it comes from the inclination of the cognizing subject, and not in any other way, not even through countless imagined alternatives.

[tal-a01-v260] Then, because of the skillful force with which that object is appropriated in its own nature, it opens up; and by that act arise determinations that follow upon its definition.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-āmarśanīyadvairūpyānudghāṭanavaśātpunaḥ / saṃśayaḥ sa kimityaṃśe vikalpastvanyathā sphuṭaḥ tenānudghāṭitātmatvabhāvaprathanameva yat / prathamaṃ sa ihoddeśaḥ praśnaḥ saṃśaya eva ca tathānudghāṭitākārabhāvaprasaravartmanā / prasarantī svasaṃvittiḥ praṣṭrī śiṣyātmatāṃ gatā tathāntaraparāmarśaniścayātmatirohiteḥ / prasarānantarodbhūtasaṃhārodayabhāgapi yāvatyeva bhavedbāhyaprasare prasphuṭātmani / anunmīlitarūpā sā praṣṭrī tāvati bhaṇyate svayamevaṃ vibodhaśca tathā praśnottarātmakaḥ / guruśiṣyapade@pyeṣa dehabhedo hyatāttvikaḥ bodho hi bodharūpatvādantarnānākṛtīḥ sthitāḥ / bahirābhāsayatyeva drāksāmānyaviśeṣataḥ srakṣyamāṇaviśeṣāṃśākāṃkṣāyogyasya kasyacit / dharmasya sṛṣṭiḥ sāmānyasṛṣṭiḥ sā saṃśayātmikā srakṣyamāṇo viśeṣāṃśo yadā tūparamettadā / nirṇayo mātṛrucito nānyathā kalpakoṭibhiḥ tasyātha vastunaḥ svātmavīryākramaṇapāṭavāt / unmudraṇaṃ tayākṛtyā lakṣaṇottaranirṇayāḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v261] Because each newly determined aspect of a property becomes the basis for what follows, examination proceeds again and again in the form of indication and definition.

[tal-a01-v262] In perception, inference, comparison, trustworthy testimony, and the rest, the triad of indication, definition, and examination shines forth in the cognition of all living beings.

[tal-a01-v263] Indication is non-conceptual, definition is conceptual construction, and examination is a further series of conceptual constructions, even within direct perception.

[tal-a01-v264] Saying 'this is a mountain' is indication; saying 'it has fire because there is smoke' is definition; and the whole network of knowledge about pervasion and the like is examination.

[tal-a01-v265] This enunciation is like a cow; the remainder becomes a definition in examination.

[tal-a01-v266] Such an enunciation, with its own desire, defines the sacrifice command; agnishtoma and the remainder are examined.

[tal-a01-v267] The creation of a thing, tolerating unwanted parts, is called enunciation.

[tal-a01-v268] Then only does one discern; future creation, arranged timelessly, connects all time.

[tal-a01-v269] The creation of what will be created and withdrawal of the previously created part, when duty is declared, is called the mark of consciousness.

[tal-a01-v270] The examination resting from creation and withdrawal is said, with a mother-approved fixed limit.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-nirṇītatāvaddharmāṃśapṛṣṭhapātitayā punaḥ / bhūyo bhūyaḥ samuddeśalakṣaṇātmaparīkṣaṇam dṛṣṭānumānaupamyāptavacanādiṣu sarvataḥ / uddeśalakṣaṇāvekṣātritayaṃ prāṇināṃ sphuret nirvikalpitamuddeśo vikalpo lakṣaṇaṃ punaḥ / parīkṣaṇaṃ tathādhyakṣe vikalpānāṃ paramparā nago@yamiti coddeśo dhūmitvādagnimāniti / lakṣyaṃ vyāptyādivijñānajālaṃ tvatra parīkṣaṇam uddeśo@yamiti prācyo gotulyo gavayābhidhaḥ / iti vā lakṣaṇaṃ śeṣaḥ parīkṣopamitau bhavet svaḥkāma īdṛguddeśo yajetetyasya lakṣaṇam / agniṣṭomādinetyeṣā parīkṣā śeṣavartinī vikalpasrakṣyamāṇānyarucitāṃśasahiṣṇunaḥ / vastuno yā tathātvena sṛṣṭiḥ soddeśasaṃjñitā tadaiva saṃviccinute yāvataḥ srakṣyamāṇatā / yato hyakālakalitā saṃdhatte sārvakālikam srakṣyamāṇasya yā sṛṣṭiḥ prāksṛṣṭāṃśasya saṃhṛtiḥ / anūdyamāne dharme sā saṃvillakṣaṇamucyate tatpṛṣṭhapātibhūyoṃśasṛṣṭisaṃhāraviśramāḥ / parīkṣā kathyate mātṛrucitā kalpitāvadhiḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v271] First seeing, then middle, then vaikhari: these are para, para-apara, and apara-natured goddesses.

[tal-a01-v272] Desire and the three powers are declared; this practice is breathed and extended.

[tal-a01-v273] In the supreme teaching, question-answer nature has fivefold relation-nature.

[tal-a01-v274] As said in Ratnamala, all is other-art-natured: great interval, divine, mixed, and fifth.

[tal-a01-v275] The unity of distinct questioner and speaker is called relation, supremacy, full-unity manifesting.

[tal-a01-v276] By this very method another relation is sufficient, scripture-declared through fullness union.

[tal-a01-v277] Thus this consciousness-goddess is by nature always the breath of three enunciations and form of all scriptures.

[tal-a01-v278] There first enunciation has elder-younger distinction; knowledge-means and supreme third means are named.

[tal-a01-v279] Shakti-means, human-means, time-means, seventh, wheel-rise, space-path, principle-path, principle-distinction.

[tal-a01-v280] Kalā-path use, power-descent concealment, initiation beginning, conventional initiation, hereditary rite.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-prākpaśyantyatha madhyānyā vaikharī ceti tā imāḥ / parā parāparā devī caramā tvaparātmikā icchādi śaktitritayamidameva nigadyate / etatprāṇita evāyaṃ vyavahāraḥ pratāyate etatpraśnottarātmatve pārameśvaraśāsane / parasaṃbandharūpatvamabhisaṃbandhapañcake yathoktaṃ ratnamālāyāṃ sarvaḥ parakalātmakaḥ / mahānavāntaro divyo miśro@nyo@nyastu pañcamaḥ bhinnayoḥ praṣṭṛtadvaktroścaikātmyaṃ yatsa ucyate / saṃbandhaḥ paratā cāsya pūrṇaikātmyaprathāmayī anenaiva nayena syātsaṃbandhāntaramapyalam / śāstravācyaṃ phalādīnāṃ paripūrṇatvayogataḥ itthaṃ saṃvidiyaṃ devī svabhāvādeva sarvadā / uddeśāditrayaprāṇā sarvaśāstrasvarūpiṇī tatrocyate puroddeśaḥ pūrvajānujabhedavān / vijñānabhidgatopāyaḥ paropāyastṛtīyakaḥ śāktopāyo naropāyaḥ kālopāyo@tha saptamaḥ / cakrodayo@tha deśādhvā tattvādhvā tattvabhedanam kalādyadhvādhvopayogaḥ śaktipātatirohitī / dīkṣopakramaṇaṃ dīkṣā sāmayī pautrike vidhau

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v281] Object-procedure, subtle initiation, immediate transcendence, balance initiation, indirect, linga-removal consecration.

[tal-a01-v282] Final rite, shraddha arrangement, remainder conduct determination, linga worship, festival purification, occasion-caused.

[tal-a01-v283] Secret practice, mantra flood, mandala, seal rite, unification, entry into own nature, scripture union.

[tal-a01-v284] Future narration and scripture-authority determination; with seven added to thirty, the wise always...

[tal-a01-v285] Practicing daily rites, he becomes directly Bhairava; in thirty-seven, complete knowledge, he becomes Bhairava.

[tal-a01-v286] What wonder, even small ones attain Bhairava-state by sight; this previous enunciation is said, now follower.

[tal-a01-v287] In the knowledge section, enunciation of bharva in order; in the second section, means-distinction.

[tal-a01-v288] Universal consciousness reflection, recollection rise order, mantra nondifference in supreme means is distinguished.

[tal-a01-v289] The refinement of conceptual thought, the principle of reasoning, the true nature of the teacher, the non-applicability of the limbs of yoga, and disregard for merely imagined worship and the like are treated here.

[tal-a01-v290] In the śākta approach, the arising of the wheel of consciousness, the true power of mantra, the real nature of recitation and related practices, and the equal standing of prohibition and injunction are discussed.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-prameyaprakriyā sūkṣmā dīkṣā sadyaḥsamutkramaḥ / tulādīkṣātha pārokṣī liṅgoddhāro@bhiṣecanam antyeṣṭiḥ śrāddhaklṛptiśca śeṣavṛttinirūpaṇam / liṅgārcā bahubhitparvapavitrādi nimittajam rahasyacaryā mantraugho maṇḍalaṃ mudrikāvidhiḥ / ekīkāraḥ svasvarūpe praveśaḥ śāstramelanam āyātikathanaṃ śāstropādeyatvanirūpaṇam / iti saptādhikāmenāṃ triṃśataṃ yaḥ sadā budhaḥ āhnikānāṃ samabhyasyet sa sākṣādbhairavo bhavet / saptatriṃśatsu saṃpūrṇabodho yadbhairavo bhavet kiṃ citramaṇavo@pyasya dṛśā bhairavatāmiyuḥ / ityeṣa pūrvajoddeśaḥ kathyate tvanujo@dhunā vijñānabhitprakaraṇe bharvasyoddeśanaṃ kramāt / dvitīyasminprakaraṇe gatopāyatvabheditā viśvacitpratibinbatvaṃ parāmarśodayakramaḥ / mantrādyabhinnarūpatvaṃ paropāye vivicyate vikalpasaṃskriyā tarkatattvaṃ gurusatattvakam / yogāṅgānupayogitvaṃ kalpitārcādyanādaraḥ saṃviccakrodayo mantravīrya japyādi vāstavam / niṣedhavidhitulyatvaṃ śāktopāye@tra carcyate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v291] Meditation of the intellect, the conscious nature of the utterance of the vital principle, and utterance as the path of entry into the supreme principle are set forth here.

[tal-a01-v292] The instrument and the principle of the phonemes are explained, and in the individual approach there is also the conceptualization of the moving cycles of day and night, transitions, and the like.

[tal-a01-v293] In the conceptualization of the path of time, there is the varied play of withdrawal and the arising of phonemes, as well as the arising of the wheel designated by the mantras and vidyās that divide that wheel.

[tal-a01-v294] The measure of the worlds and their summary correlation with the principles are treated in the account of the path of space, and a corresponding pair is treated in the determination of the path of principles.

[tal-a01-v295] The relation of cause and effect, the explanation of the sequence of principles, the nature of reality, the classification of principles, and the explanation of waking and the other states are all treated here.

[tal-a01-v296] In the division of the principles, the division of cognizing subjects is examined, along with the nature of kalā and the ways the principles are grouped as one, three, five, and so forth.

[tal-a01-v297] The sequence of the divisions of the phonemes and the explanation of the all-supporting power are analyzed to this extent within the investigation of the paths beginning with kalā.

[tal-a01-v298] In the application of the paths, the contemplation of non-difference, along with trembling and laughter, is treated, as well as the multiplication of impurities, their true nature, and the manifold variety of power.

[tal-a01-v299] In the examination of the descent of power, the establishment of independence and the manifold variety of concealment are the topics summarized for discussion.

[tal-a01-v300] At the commencement of initiation, concealment is removed through knowledge, fullness is attained, and departure from the body is shown to be unnecessary.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-buddhidhyānaṃ prāṇatattvasamuccāraścidātmatā / uccāraḥ paratattvāntaḥpraveśapathalakṣaṇam karaṇaṃ varṇatattvaṃ cetyāṇave tu nirūpyate / cāramānamahorātrasaṃkrāntyādivikalpanam saṃhāracitratā varṇodayaḥ kālādhvakalpane / cakrabhinmantravidyābhidetaccakrodaye bhavet parimāṇaṃ purāṇāṃ ca saṃgrahastattvayojanam / etaddeśādhvanirdeśe dvayaṃ tattvādhvanirṇaye kāryakāraṇabhāvaśca tattvakramanirūpaṇam / vastudharmastattvavidhirjāgradādinirūpaṇam pramātṛbheda ityetat tattvabhede vicāryate / kalāsvarūpamekatripañcādyaistattvakalpanam varṇabhedakramaḥ sarvādhāraśaktinirūpaṇam / kalādyadhvavicārāntaretāvatpravivicyate abhedabhāvanākampahāsau tvadhvopayojane / saṃkhyādhikyaṃ malādīnāṃ tattvaṃ śaktivicitratā anapekṣitvasiddhiśca tirobhāvavicitratā / śaktipātaparīkṣāyāmetāvānvācyasaṃgrahaḥ tirobhāvavyapagamo jñānena paripūrṇatā / utkrāntyanupayogitvaṃ dīkṣopakramaṇe sthitam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v301] In the examination of the student's fitness and related matters, the conception of places divided by location, the division of general nyāsa, the offering vessel, and their purpose are covered.

[tal-a01-v302] The fitness of materials, worship, outer-door worship, sequential entry, the nature of initiation, and the purification of body, breath, and so on are outlined.

[tal-a01-v303] The variety of special nyāsa, the special offering vessel, worship of the body, and nyāsa and worship on the paths of breath, intellect, and consciousness are described.

[tal-a01-v304] The superiority over other scriptural groups, worship of the wheel on all sides, taking possession of the site, the five cow products, and worship of the earth and Gaṇeśa are included.

[tal-a01-v305] Worship of the weapon mantra, the fire rite, consecration related to fire, oblations of satisfaction, preparation of the rice offering, and rites ending with the tooth-stick are treated.

[tal-a01-v306] The rite of Śiva's hand, preparation of the bed, rites relating to dreams, and the observances are summarized.

[tal-a01-v307] In the fifteenth chapter, on the rite of becoming an initiate, contemplation of the self of the maṇḍala and the elaboration of the offered victim are covered.

[tal-a01-v308] Satisfaction of the fire, illumination of one's own nature, the rite of nyāsa on the paths present in the student's body, and the variety of what is purified, the purifier, and so on are treated.

[tal-a01-v309] In the sixteenth chapter, the division of initiation, the supreme nyāsa, the purpose of the being of mantra, and the division of yojanikā and related matters are presented.
