[tal-a01-v310] In the rite of the son's initiation, the preparation of the thread, purification of the principles, burning of the bonds, application, and the division of the paths are stated.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-śiṣyaucityaparīkṣādau sthānabhitsthānakalpanam / sāmānyanyāsabhedo@rghapātraṃ caitatprayojanam dravyayogyatvamarcā ca bahirdvārārcanaṃ kramāt / praveśo diksvarūpaṃ ca dehaprāṇādiśodhanam viśeṣanyāsavaicitryaṃ saviśeṣārghabhājanam / dehapūjā prāṇabuddhicitsvadhvanyāsapūjane anyaśāstragaṇotkarṣaḥ pūjā cakrasya sarvataḥ / kṣetragrahaḥ pañcagavyaṃ pūjanaṃ bhūgaṇeśayoḥ astrārcā vahnikāryaṃ cāpyadhivāsanamagnigam / tarpaṇaṃ carusaṃsiddhirdantakāṣṭhāntasaṃskriyā śivahastavidhiścāpi śayyāklṛptivicāraṇam / svapnasya sāmayaṃ karma samayāśceti saṃgrahaḥ samayitvavidhāvasminsyātpañcadaśa āhnike / maṇḍalātmānusandhānaṃ nivedyapaśuvistaraḥ agnitṛptiḥ svasvabhāvadīpanaṃ śiṣyadehagaḥ / adhvanyāsavidhiḥ śodhyaśodhakādivicitratā dīkṣābhedaḥ paro nyāso mantrasattāprayojanam / bhedo yojanikādeśca ṣoḍaśe syādihāhnike sūtraklṛptistattvaśuddhiḥ pāśadāho@tha yojanam / adhvabhedastathetyevaṃ kathitaṃ pautrike vidhau

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v311] In the eighteenth chapter, called the abbreviated initiation, the absence of birth and the like and a very clear division of mantras are treated.

[tal-a01-v312] In the rite of immediate departure, inspection of kalā, nyāsa of the sword and the like, movement occurring in the body, and the rite of brahma-vidyā are taught.

[tal-a01-v313] In the twentieth chapter, the full subject to be explained will be consecration ending with the examination of qualification, and also the rite of the balance.

[tal-a01-v314] In the twenty-first chapter, the procedures to be explained are the rite of the dead and the living, the net, lordship over positions, the group of consecratory rites, and the examination of strength and weakness.

[tal-a01-v315] In the procedure for removing the mark, what must be clearly explained is hearing, permission, purification, the removal of sin, and the cutting off of doubt.

[tal-a01-v316] The examination and appointment of the teacher, his vow, the removal of the disciple's understanding, its divisions, and the state of being a sādhaka in the rite of consecration—this much is to be covered.

[tal-a01-v317] The qualified person, the consecration, and its purpose—this is what is to be explained and discussed in the twenty-fourth chapter, called the final worship.

[tal-a01-v318] In the twenty-fifth chapter, in the exposition of śrāddha, the purpose—granting enjoyment and liberation—and the procedure are made clear, and the topics are summarized.

[tal-a01-v319] The purpose of the remaining conduct, daily worship, the supreme worship on the altar, the nature of the liṅga in its many forms, and the explanation of the rosary are to be set forth.

[tal-a01-v320] The divisions of worship are to be explained in the revelation of liṅga worship, and then the division, purpose, and procedure of occasional rites.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-jananādivihīnatvaṃ mantrabhedo@tha susphuṭaḥ / iti saṃkṣiptadīkṣākhye syādaṣṭādaśa āhnike kalāvekṣā kṛpāṇyādinyāsaścāraḥ śarīragaḥ / brahmavidyāvidhiścaivamuktaṃ sadyaḥsamutkrame adhikāraparīkṣāntaḥsaṃskāro@tha tulāvidhiḥ / ityetadvācyasarvasvaṃ syādviṃśatitamāhnike mṛtajīvadvidhirjālo padeśaḥ saṃskriyāgaṇaḥ / balābalavicāraścetyekaviṃśāhnike vidhiḥ śravaṇaṃ cābhyanujñānaṃ śodhanaṃ pātakacyutiḥ / śaṅkāccheda iti spaṣṭaṃ vācyaṃ liṅgoddhṛtikrame parīkṣācāryakaraṇaṃ tadvrataṃ haraṇaṃ mateḥ / tadvibhāgaḥ sādhakatvamabhiṣekavidhau tviyat adhikāryatha saṃskārastatprayojanamityadaḥ / caturviṃśe@ntyayāgākhye vaktavyaṃ paricarcyate prayojanaṃ bhogamokṣadānenātra vidhiḥ sphuṭaḥ / pañcaviṃśāhnike śrāddhaprakāśe vastusaṃgrahaḥ prayojanaṃ śeṣavṛtternityārcā sthaṇḍile parā / liṅgasvarūpaṃ bahudhā cākṣasūtranirūpaṇam pūjābheda iti vācyaṃ liṅgārcāsaṃprakāśane / naimittikavibhāgastatprayojanavidhistataḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a01-v321] The divisions of festivals, their specifics, circle worship and its performance, and the purpose of worship on guru days and other special beginning and end days are to be explained.

[tal-a01-v322] The examination of death, the procedure for gatherings of yoginīs and others, the method of exposition, the method of hearing, and the procedure for guru worship are to be described.

[tal-a01-v323] In the twenty-eighth chapter, called the revelation of occasional rites, are established the division of the qualified practitioner and the sequence of the lineage of siddhas and their consorts.

[tal-a01-v324] In the twenty-ninth chapter are the procedures of worship and of the messenger, the sequence of the secret upaniṣad, initiation, consecration, and awakening.

[tal-a01-v325] In the thirtieth chapter, the nature of mantra and its power are explained. In the thirty-first, the division of the trident and lotus and the explanation of the sky, the swastika, and so on are to be set forth in detail.

[tal-a01-v326] These matters are to be explained in detail in the thirty-first chapter. In the thirty-second chapter are set forth the distinctions of quality and principality, their own nature, and the worship of their power.

[tal-a01-v327] The division of kalā is declared in the full revelation of the seals, because from the thirty-two principles up to Īśa it becomes clearly manifest there.

[tal-a01-v328] Since there is no separate division here, no additional topic is stated in this overview. Even so, that matter is treated because it is primary and must be known in the sequence of another section.

[tal-a01-v329] Thus the method of enunciation has been declared for the sake of easy comprehension. Now, in examining its characteristics, they will be explained in due order.

[tal-a01-v330] The self abides as partless consciousness-light, and its own nature is the host of powers of consciousness. It appears bound by concealing its own greatness, and its liberation comes through revealing its luminous nature. This manifold meaning has been briefly revealed here.

[tal-a01-v331] False knowledge produces defects of vision like a cataract, so that even what is pure seems to be a place of impurity. But when that cataract-like defect in vision is recognized and removed, how could any suspicion of impurity remain?

[tal-a01-v332] O host of beings, you forcibly seize people's hearts, make them dance with many gestures, conceal the heart of the self, and sport in that way. Whoever calls you insentient is himself insentient and poorly taught in thinking himself sensitive; I would even take his insentience as a kind of praise, since it suggests a likeness to you.

[tal-a01-v333] Here, teachers whose impurities have fallen away, who know the higher and the lower, and who are grounded in the true being of Shiva are authorized to undertake investigation. Without that qualification, inquiry is fruitless and leads only to hatred, blame, loss, and begging.
